source_text:
Ἐάν με καταξιώσῃ Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ ὑμῶν καὶ θέλημα ᾖ, ἐν τῷ δευτέρῳ βιβλιδίῳ, ὃ μέλλω γράφειν ὑμῖν, προσδηλώσω ὑμῖν, ἦς ἠρξάμην οἰκονομίας εἰς τὸν καινὸν ἄνθρωπον Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, ἐν τῇ αὐτοῦ πίστει καὶ ἐν τῇ αὐτοῦ ἀγάπῃ, ἐν πάθει αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀναστάσει:
μάλιστα ἐὰν ὁ κύριός μοι ἀποκαλύψῃ, ὅτι οἱ κατ’ ἄνδρα κοινῇ πάντες ἐν χάριτι ἐξ ὀνόματος συνέρχεσθε ἐν μιᾷ πίστει καὶ ἐν Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ. τῷ κατὰ σάρκα ἐκ γένους Δαυείδ, τῷ υἱῷ ἀνθρώπου καὶ υἱῷ θεοῦ, εἰς τὸ ὑπακούειν ὑμᾶς τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ καὶ τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ ἀπερισπάστῳ διανοίᾳ, ἕνα ἄρτον κλῶντες, ὅς ἐστιν φάρμακον ἀθανασίας, ἀντίδοτος τοῦ μὴ ἀποθανεῖν, ἀλλὰ ζῆν ἐν Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ διὰ παντός.
thought_title: The second letter and the medicine of immortality
orientation: Ignatius is closing his letter to the Ephesians, promising a second letter and describing the unity he hopes to hear about among them.
pass_a_gloss: If Jesus Christ considers me worthy in the prayer of you and [it] is [his] will, in the second little book, which I am about to write to you, I will make clear further to you, of which I began the plan for the new man Jesus Christ, in his faith and in his love, in his passion and resurrection: especially if the Lord reveals to me, that you all man by man together in grace by name come together in one faith and in Jesus Christ. [to him] who according to flesh [is] from the race of David, [to him] the son of man and son of God, so that you obey the bishop and the council of elders with undistracted mind, breaking one bread, which is the medicine of immortality, the antidote of not dying, but of living in Jesus Christ through all.

choices.why: The diminutive is deliberate; Ignatius calls his planned second letter a small writing, not a formal treatise.
Here it refers to God's saving arrangement centered on Christ, not household management.
The distributive phrase stresses individual participation, not just a collective gathering.
The metaphor is medicinal; the bread is a remedy that confers immortal life.
Keeps the medical metaphor parallel to 'medicine' and preserves the infinitive's force.
rejected: antidote so as not to die

choices.why: The adjective describes a mind not pulled away by other concerns, matching Ignatius's emphasis on single-minded obedience.

pass_b_english: If Jesus Christ considers me worthy through your prayers, and if it is His will, I will explain to you in the second little book that I intend to write to you the plan I have begun to set forth concerning the new man, Jesus Christ, in His faith and in His love, in His passion and resurrection.

I will do this especially if the Lord reveals to me that you all, man by man, come together by name in grace, in one faith and in Jesus Christ, who according to the flesh is from the line of David, the son of man and Son of God, so that you obey the bishop and the council of elders with undistracted mind, breaking one bread, which is the medicine of immortality, the antidote so that we do not die but live in Jesus Christ forever.

problems.why: Pass B lacks sentence shape; polish into readable prose without adding claims

edits.old: If Jesus Christ considers me worthy through your prayers, and if it is His will, I will make clear to you in the second little book that I intend to write to you the plan I have begun for the new man Jesus Christ, in His faith and in His love, in His passion and resurrection—especially if the Lord reveals to me that you all, man by man, come together by name in grace, in one faith and in Jesus Christ, who according to the flesh is from the line of David, the son of man and Son of God, so that you obey the bishop and the council of elders with undistracted mind, breaking one bread, which is the medicine of immortality, the antidote against dying, but living in Jesus Christ forever.
edits.new: If Jesus Christ considers me worthy through your prayers, and if it is His will, I will make clear to you in the second little book that I intend to write to you the plan I have begun for the new man Jesus Christ, in His faith and in His love, in His passion and resurrection. This I will do especially if the Lord reveals to me that you all, man by man, come together by name in grace, in one faith and in Jesus Christ, who according to the flesh is from the line of David, the son of man and Son of God, so that you obey the bishop and the council of elders with undistracted mind, breaking one bread, which is the medicine of immortality, the antidote against dying, but living in Jesus Christ forever.

fixed: The source has a long sentence; the English was one long sentence. I split it into two sentences to improve readability without adding claims.

problems.quote: I will explain to you in the second little book that I intend to write to you the plan I have begun for the new man Jesus Christ
problems.why: Syntax is tangled; reader cannot parse what 'the plan I have begun for the new man' means.
problems.fix: Rephrase: 'I will explain the plan I have begun concerning the new man, Jesus Christ.'

edits.old: I will explain to you in the second little book that I intend to write to you the plan I have begun for the new man Jesus Christ
edits.new: I will explain to you in the second little book that I intend to write to you the plan I have begun concerning the new man, Jesus Christ

problems.why: Two different metaphors for Eucharist in same sentence; 'medicine' and 'antidote' are not identical concepts, though both translate Greek pharmakon.
problems.fix: Note that both translate same word, or choose one with explanation.

problems.why: 'Little book' (biblidion) suggests a short work, but reader may think of a physical booklet; Ignatius means a future letter.
problems.fix: Add note: 'little book' = second letter he plans to write.

edits.old: which is the medicine of immortality, the antidote against dying
edits.new: which is the medicine of immortality, the antidote that keeps us from dying

fixed: The 'medicine of immortality' and 'antidote' issue is not a mistranslation: both render the same Greek word pharmakon, and the English already preserves the two complementary metaphors. No change needed.
The phrase 'second little book' is a faithful rendering of biblidion and the context already makes clear it refers to a future letter; no change needed.

problems.why: 'Council of elders' is standard, but 'council of the apostles' and 'council of the bishop' appear once each; reader may miss these are the same institution.
problems.fix: Use consistent 'council of elders' with note where source differs.

problems.quote: the plan I have begun concerning the new man, Jesus Christ, in His faith and in His love, in His passion and resurrection
problems.why: 'Plan I have begun' is unclear—did Ignatius begin a plan or a treatise? 'In His faith' is ambiguous (Christ's faith or ours?).
problems.fix: 'Plan I have begun' → 'the plan of the new man...which I have begun to set forth.'

edits.old: the plan I have begun concerning the new man, Jesus Christ, in His faith and in His love, in His passion and resurrection.
edits.new: the plan of the new man, Jesus Christ, which I have begun to set forth, in His faith and in His love, in His passion and resurrection.

fixed: The glossary issue is not a translation error; 'council of elders' is the correct rendering of πρεσβυτερίῳ here, and the source does not contain 'council of the apostles' or 'council of the bishop' in this section.

The source reads ἦς ἠρξάμην οἰκονομίας εἰς τὸν καινὸν ἄνθρωπον Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, where οἰκονομίας is the plan and ἦς ἠρξάμην means 'which I began.' The English 'the plan I have begun concerning the new man' misplaces the relative clause; the plan is 'of the new man,' and 'which I have begun' modifies the plan. The edit clarifies this without changing the meaning.

last_rejected.quote: the plan I have begun for the new man Jesus Christ
last_rejected.source_quote: ἦς ἠρξάμην οἰκονομίας εἰς τὸν καινὸν ἄνθρωπον Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν
last_rejected.why: οἰκονομίας is 'dispensation/economy', not 'plan'; 'new man' is Christ himself, not a plan 'for' him.
last_rejected.fix: the dispensation I have begun for the new man, Jesus Christ
last_rejected.ruling: οἰκονομία can mean 'plan'; εἰς with accusative 'for' is reasonable. Not a clear major error.

last_rejected.quote: come together by name in grace
last_rejected.why: ἐξ ὀνόματος means 'by name' in sense of 'personally/individually', but 'by name in grace' obscures that each comes personally into grace.
last_rejected.fix: come together, each by name, in grace
last_rejected.ruling: ἐξ ὀνόματος rendered 'by name' is within normal range; meaning not clearly changed or lost.

last_rejected.quote: the antidote against dying, but living in Jesus Christ forever
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀντίδοτος τοῦ μὴ ἀποθανεῖν, ἀλλὰ ζῆν ἐν Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ διὰ παντός
last_rejected.why: The antidote is 'so as not to die, but to live'—infinitives of purpose; English makes 'living' a separate clause, losing the purpose construction.
last_rejected.fix: the antidote so as not to die, but to live in Jesus Christ forever
last_rejected.ruling: English 'against dying, but living' adequately conveys ἀντίδοτος τοῦ μὴ ἀποθανεῖν ἀλλὰ ζῆν; purpose sense preserved.

polish.changed: Clarified the conditional structure and pronoun references, kept the Eucharistic imagery intact, and ensured the sentence flows naturally for modern readers while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.why: Reader may not realize 'council of elders' = 'elders' = presbyterion, and 'council of the apostles' is a typological parallel, not a different group.
notes.fix: Use consistent 'council of elders' with note; clarify 'council of the apostles' as typology.

notes.why: 'Passible' (capable of suffering) vs 'passion' (suffering/death) are related but distinct; reader may miss Christological point.
notes.fix: Gloss 'passible' as 'capable of suffering' on first use.

notes.why: Reader may think 'council of the apostles' is a historical body separate from 'council of elders', not realizing it's a typological parallel.
notes.fix: Add note: 'council of the apostles' typologically parallels 'council of elders'.

notes.quote: council of elders of the church

variants.text: council of elders of the church

notes.why: Same entity as 'council of elders' elsewhere; 'of the church' adds no distinction but may confuse.
Same Eucharistic image in same sentence; reader may think these are two different things.
notes.fix: Clarify these are two metaphors for the Eucharist, not distinct elements.

notes.why: Same office rendered two ways; readers may think 'elders' are different from 'council of elders.'

polish.changed: Clarified that the plan concerns the new man Jesus Christ, made the subject of the plan explicit, and smoothed the sentence flow while preserving every claim and Scripture reference.

notes.quote: the plan of the new man, Jesus Christ
notes.why: 'New man' is a technical theological phrase (Ephesians 2:15) left unexplained.
notes.fix: Note this echoes Eph 2:15, the new humanity created in Christ.
